title: Phase 3 QA
eyebrow: QA · roadmap phase 3 (#495) and feature switches (#535) · plugin 2.81.0 on AjsAgent/phase-3-handoff

short.lead: Phase 3 and the feature switches are built on the branch AjsAgent/phase-3-handoff as plugin 2.81.0: fourteen build steps, and four older issues to be closed with evidence instead of rebuilt. The hook check script (verify.py) passes 1247 of 1247 checks, the tools check (tools/verify_tools.py) passes 54 of 54, and the doc drift check finds 0 out-of-date citations. Real Claude sessions ran without a screen (headless), using only this branch's plugin. They saved work, picked it up in a second folder, and turned the page reminders off in a folder outside git. Reviewing the helper agents' work found and fixed seven problems before anything merged (see the Review found row). Your 2026-11-17 choice, that a save holds every new file git does not ignore, is built too. What is left needs you: a second Claude account, your Windows PC, and a real cloud session.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what was run and what it showed.
items: Every branch is saved, one save per folder

Live: a session created notes.txt and did not commit. Afterwards the test's stand-in for GitHub (a local copy playing its part) held a hidden save, refs/house-rules/saves/AjsAgent/live/e9979774. The save contained notes.txt and a facts file. The facts file named the branch, the branch's latest commit and the unsaved files. The branch itself got no new commit. verify.py proves two clones keep two saves, and that an old autosave/<branch> save cannot block a new one. Build steps 1 and 3 (issues #527 and #529). Since your choice on 2026-11-17, a save holds every new file git does not ignore, however it was made. A git-ignored file stays out, and a file over 50 MB is left out and named.
A cloud session commits to its own branch

Live, with the cloud-session setting CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true: on branch ajsagent/live, the branch on the stand-in for GitHub got a commit named "wip: autosave" holding notes.txt, and no hidden save was pushed. On the main branch, the save never commits. It was also run against real GitHub, from this cloud container. On the throwaway branch ajsagent/phase-3-live-cloud-2, a session made notes.txt with a shell command. The save committed and pushed it (commit ab9f2de on GitHub). A fresh clone from GitHub had the file. Step 2, issue #528.
A new folder opens with where the work stood

Live: a session in a second clone listed notes.txt from the first folder's save, the handoff note, and the restore command git diff <save>^ <save> -- notes.txt | git apply. Running that command brought back notes.txt, which contained "hello". The session-start hook never restores anything itself. Step 5, issue #531.
A reply that leaves work unsaved is sent back once

Checked by verify.py. Each of these gets the reply sent back once: a branch not pushed, a handoff note older than the newest commit, a note holding a page or session link, and a turn that changed files without updating Today.md. The retry never blocks the reply. Step 4, issue #530.
Type a switch in any folder

Live: "pages off" in a folder outside git saved {"pages":"off"} there; the next prompt carried the Pages OFF note, and a control folder did not. A control reply of 395 words got the page reminder; with pages off it did not. A quoted "should I type pages off?" saved nothing. verify.py also proves three things. A switch set "everywhere" applies in a second folder. A switch set for one folder overrides it. With "house rules off", the guard still refuses git reset --hard and a commit on main. Issues #536 to #538.
One command switches the plugin build

tools/verify_tools.py, in a throwaway config folder: switching to AjsAgent/phase-3-handoff installed that branch's commit, and main switched back. A switch to a branch that does not exist exits 1 and puts the normal build back. Step 6, #532.
Seven fixes built, four closed with evidence

Fixed, each with a test that failed first: verify.py --only (#44); the settings block at the top of agent files (#46); a command starting with & (#137); a warning when Python is missing (#205). A merged phase pull request now closes its step issues (#520); this cloud session read the parent issue of #531 live. The docs-tiers note offers instead of orders (#521), and switching branch then committing works in one command (#522). Already fixed, and to be closed with evidence after QA: #202 (the docref check), #215 (guard checks after 5 minutes), #515 (the close guard with the loop off) and #409 (quoted approvals).

1: a save name that git could not nest under an old save (renamed to refs/house-rules/saves/). 2: the Today.md rule dropped from the end-of-reply check (restored). 3: a guard loophole, git switch -c AjsAgent/x && git checkout main && git commit (now refused). 4: switching to a branch build could leave you with no plugin installed (a failed switch now puts the normal build back). 5: the pickup's fetches could hit its 15-second limit (raised to 25). 6: a flaky approval test, timestamps a second apart (fixed). 7: the new rule sentence pushed the rules loaded at session start to 9798 characters, over the 9700 limit (shortened to 9675, detail moved).
Thirteen steps on your PC, one action each

The steps are step cards, with the exact command, where to run it and what you should see: docs/plans/2026-11-17-phase-3-qa-steps.md in this repo, and in my chat message. They cover switching to this build, a pickup from your first Claude account to your second, the pages switch in a folder outside git, the Windows test run for #523, and switching back.
All 13 steps, then your verdict and the FAIL lines from step 12.

unverified: A second Claude account: every run here used this session's one account
Your Windows PC: every run was Linux in this cloud container, and #523's 8 Windows-only failures are not fixed yet
A turn really cut off by a usage limit: only replayed test inputs have run. (Claude Code sends a StopFailure event when a turn ends on an error.)
Whether a cloud session follows a branch build: tools/use_branch.py was tested for your user settings only
